title: Yohanan ben Toratah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Pesikta Rabbati, Parah 3, relates that a Jew sold his cow to a gentile, who plowed with it throughout the week. On Shabbat it refused to plow, being accustomed to rest, and the buyer wanted to undo the sale. The Jew whispered in the cow’s ears: while it was his, it rested on Shabbat, but now that it belonged to a gentile it had to work. The buyer feared sorcery, but the Jew explained truthfully what he had said. The buyer converted, studied and attained Torah learning; they called him Yohanan ben Toratah. Seder HaDorot attributes the story to Rabbi Chanina ben Torata.

notes.text: Toratah is used for Yohanan in both heading and story; Torata belongs to the separate Chanina attribution in Seder HaDorot. The narrative does not by itself authorize an identity merger with another ben Torta.

The complete cow narrative was directly read in the consulted digital Pesikta Rabbati chapter 14. Hyman’s supplied locator is Parah 3; this consultation does not establish that subsection scheme or identify Yohanan with the Chanina ben Torata whom Hyman reports from Seder HaDorot.
